title: Sephiria Beginner Guide: Side Bag, New Events, First 12 Runs
description: Sephiria beginner guide and walkthrough: first-run priorities, Side Bag rules, Destiny New Events, and combat habits for 1.0.
meta: First 12 runs: Side Bag stays inactive, do Destiny New Events, commit to 1–2 combo tags.
body:
Sephiria throws systems at you fast. Treat the first dozen runs as unlocking the Destiny tree and learning one build sentence—not chasing every shiny Artifact.

Core loop

  • Pick a costume and weapon, enter a floor, choose nodes (Anvil / Dice / combat / shops).
  • Spend Sapphires after runs on the Destiny Inscription permanent tree.
  • Open the Journal (Esc) to review unlocked weapons, Artifacts, Tablets, and Miracles before committing.

First-run priorities

  • Do New Events on the Destiny tree—they unlock systems (wishing fountain, costumes salon, weapons) that snowball later.
  • Prefer Anvil early so your weapon skill matches the build you are forcing.
  • Side Bag is not free power—items stored there are inactive (including Tablets).
  • Commit to 1–2 combo tags (Storm Cloud, Companion, Glacier, etc.). Diluting five tags starves Tablet payoffs.
Steam Community “Basic Guide” still helps for systems vocabulary, but prefer 1.0-era writeups for route advice after the July 31, 2026 full release.

Side Bag: stored items are inactive

Items in the Side Bag do not contribute their effects, including Tablets. Move the pieces your build needs into the active inventory, then check their adjacency. Use the Side Bag for storage rather than counting it as another active equipment slot. See Artifacts and Tablets for the inventory layout.

Combat habits that transfer

  • Perfect Guard saves huge MP versus holding block.
  • Reorganize inventory after bosses—adjacency and Tablet geometry matter more than raw rarity.
  • Fruit Skewers bias which combo families appear; frozen fruit can suppress junk families.

Related Sephiria guides

  • Destiny Inscription tree — spend your first sapphires well
  • Sephiria builds — your first real build
  • Hard Mode unlock — what comes after a first clear

The run loop, in four moves

MoveQuestion to answerMistake it prevents
ReadWhat is the nearest threat, what is its attack cue, and where can I retreat?Committing to a long sequence with no exit
CommitWhat is the shortest safe attack sequence that still moves the fight forward?Greeding damage you cannot recover from
CollectWhat does this reward change in the plan I already have?Starting a second unrelated build mid-run
RebuildWhich Artifact and Tablet moves make the next fight easier?Carrying a stale board into a boss

Name the problem before taking the reward

What the run is doingWhat to takeWhat not to take
Enemies survive too longStrengthen a damage source you can actually landA new conditional effect that needs different habits
Mistakes drain healthDefence, recovery, control, a safer rhythmAnother damage tag you cannot keep active
The core already worksUptime and Tablet placement for the existing effectsA fresh unrelated plan
Nothing activates reliablySimplify — keep the clearest triggerMore promises this run cannot fulfil

Source: community beginner walkthrough for 1.0 (sephiria.net), checked 9 November 2026. The framing is theirs; the decision to keep or cut a tag is still yours to make against your own board.

After the run ends

Split the cause into one of five buckets — positioning, an unread attack, weak damage, poor recovery, or an effect that never activated — then change exactly one answer next time. Changing three things at once hides which one worked. Spend the post-run currency on the Destiny tree before chasing another weapon unlock, because the tree is what carries between runs.
